physicalNotes: Radius 0.05049522 Jupiter radii from Tey et al. 2024 (2024AJ....167..283T), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..283T/abstract): 3,610 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.000398 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 1.744698366 d
sources.shape: Tey et al. 2024 (2024AJ....167..283T), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname TEY_ET_AL__2024): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.02123 au and stellar radius 0.4314 solar radii; Tey et al. 2024 (2024AJ....167..283T), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname TEY_ET_AL__2024): inclination 89.99 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2460985.903551 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 2 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
